workstream: 12. Separate Alia product plans from Oxy financial billing
checkbox: Audit every Alia plan, credit, subscription and transaction path.
note: data-billing.json inventories the seven TABLES. This file inventories the PATHS that write them: every writer, every caller of that writer, and which half of ADR 0005's split the write belongs to. Re-derived and asserted by packages/api/src/__tests__/billingSeparation.test.ts, which fails on a writer or a caller this file does not name AND on one it names that no longer exists.

method.writers: Every exported function declared under packages/api/src/db/billing/ whose body reaches db.insert()/update()/delete() on one of the seven tables, found through the TypeScript AST. An AST rather than grep: a comment quoting a call reads identical to the call, and db/schema/billing.ts names addCredits in prose.
method.callers: Every non-test module OUTSIDE db/billing/ that imports that writer by name, static or awaited-dynamic, resolving an `as` alias back to the exported name.
method.residual: Every site the census does not claim is explained rather than dropped. One false positive was found and resolved this way: a grep for seedPlanFeatures reports internal/providers/lib/seed-model-configs.ts:271, which imports a DIFFERENT function of the same name from ./seed-features.js — the seeder wrapper, not the repository writer. The AST census attributes it correctly and the grep does not.
method.positiveControl: The scanner is pinned against a literal buffer containing one writing and one non-writing exported function, so an empty result cannot pass as a clean one. Its floor in the live tree is 27 writers over 7 tables, asserted exactly. It was 26 until #139 ws14 added setPlanModelIds; the number is read off the scan rather than incremented, because arithmetic on a measurement is how a plausible wrong one lands.

classification.CATALOGUE: What is for sale. A product concept ADR 0005 leaves with Alia; it survives cutover unchanged.
classification.ENTITLEMENT: What an account may do and how much of its allowance is left. The low-latency read model, also Alia's.
classification.FINANCIAL: What a customer was charged or owes. Oxy's under ADR 0001/0005; these paths are what workstream 12 removes, and they are BLOCKED_OXY_972 until Oxy is authoritative.

finding.userCreditsIsTheOnlySharedTable: Six of the seven tables fall wholly on one side. `user_credits` does not: `credits_free` is the daily allowance (ENTITLEMENT) and `credits_paid` is bought or granted balance (FINANCIAL), in one row. The split runs through addCredits's `type` argument rather than through the table, which is why a table-level inventory cannot see it and this path-level one can. At cutover the FINANCIAL writers of this table are the ones that go; the ENTITLEMENT writers stay.
finding.unreachableWriters: 12 of the 27 writers have no caller anywhere in the package. Eleven are the catalogue's insert/update/delete set, orphaned when the never-mounted /internal/gateway admin routes were deleted (see db/schema/CONVENTIONS.md on deleteProviderKey, the same event). The twelfth is spendCreditsPaidFirst, which userCreditsRepository.ts keeps deliberately — it is the ported `deductCredits`, spending PAID first, and the file says it is named apart so the difference from spendCreditsFreeFirst cannot be collapsed by accident. Unreachable is recorded, not repaired: this audit's job is to say which paths exist, and a writer nothing calls is a fact about the cutover's blast radius.
finding.priceLivesOnTheAliasToo: A reader looking for where Alia's price lives will find `plans.monthly_price` and `credit_packages.price` and stop, and be wrong. What a REQUEST costs a customer is `alia_models.credit_multiplier`: lib/credits-manager.ts:52 reads it off the resolved alias inside getCreditMultiplier, and every credit figure — chat, voice, images, audio — is that multiplier times a token or minute count. So the alias catalogue is a third price surface beside the two obvious ones, and it is the one on the request path. Two consequences for the cutover: retiring an alias from ADVERTISED surfaces must leave it RESOLVING, because the multiplier is read after resolution; and moving product pricing to Oxy is not finished when `plans` and `credit_packages` move, because the per-request rate is not in either of them. It is still not upstream cost — `cost_entries.cost_usd` is that, in a different table with no shared reader (see the disjointness gate) — so this widens where product price lives without weakening the separation from provider cost.
finding.singleStripeSurface: Every FINANCIAL write outside the credit balance enters through routes/billing.ts. There is exactly one Stripe webhook surface (POST /billing/webhook) and one Stripe client (getStripe, lib/stripe-prices.ts shares it by parameter), which is what makes `Remove duplicate Stripe webhooks` a one-file change when Oxy is authoritative.
finding.noBillingWriteEmitsAnAuditRecord: MEASURED, and now true of 26 of the 27 writers rather than all of them. #167 added an audit-record mechanism that fires from INSIDE the repository function, with a required `actor` and a per-resource field allow-list, over five tables: alia_models, alia_model_provider_mappings, model_configs, provider_keys, external_models. #139 ws14 added a sixth resource, `plan`, and exactly one billing writer emits a record: `setPlanModelIds`, reached from PUT /internal/plans/:planId/models. That is not a billing audit trail and is not meant as one — it is there because `plans.model_ids` is the input to lib/plan-access.ts and therefore decides which MODEL a request may name, which is exactly #167's subject wearing a billing table's name. Every other column of `plans`, and every write to the other six tables, still emits nothing: there is no answer to `who changed this plan's price` or `who granted these credits` beyond the application log. That was deliberately NOT extended: no checkbox in workstream 12 asks for a billing audit trail. Recorded as a follow-up candidate rather than done, with what it would buy: an actor-attributed record on `addCredits`, `insertTransaction` and the two subscription writers would make a disputed balance answerable from the database instead of from log retention, and it would survive the cutover as the Alia-side half of a reconciliation against Oxy's ledger. If it is ever wanted, extend #167's mechanism as ws14 did — a second one would be a second vocabulary for the same question.

tables.note: What is offered. Carries Stripe product and price ids, which are a POINTER to the processor's catalogue rather than a charge — updatePlanByPlanId writes only those three columns.

writers.entrypoint: boot seed, called from src/index.ts startBackgroundServices. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING for the whole row, model_ids included: which models a plan grants is owned at runtime by setPlanModelIds (#139 ws14), so a boot writer that re-asserted the list would revert it on every deploy. It used to rewrite model_ids wholesale and nothing ran it, which is why the reversion was never observed.

PUT /internal/plans/:planId/models, behind oxyServiceAuth (#139 ws14). The only runtime writer of plans.model_ids, which lib/plan-access.ts reads to decide whether a request may name a model. Writes that one column and no other — it takes a list, not an updates object — and emits a config-audit record with a required actor. Touches no amount and no Stripe id. Plus scripts/plan-models.ts, the operator one-shot that re-asserts the seeded list against a row created before a model existed — seedPlan is onConflictDoNothing, so without it a stale model list cannot be corrected at all.

lib/stripe-prices.ts ensureStripePriceId, reached from POST /billing/checkout/subscription and POST /billing/subscription/change-plan. Persists an auto-created Stripe product/price id onto the plan; writes no amount.

tables.note: Capabilities a plan may grant, for the pricing table. No money anywhere in the row.
The junction, and the source of every ALLOWANCE the entitlement read model publishes: a row with a limit_value becomes a contract PlanAllowance, a row without one becomes a boolean capability.

writers.entrypoint: boot seed, imported there as insertSeedPlanFeatures. NOT the same function as seed-features.ts's own exported seedPlanFeatures, which seed-model-configs.ts calls — see method.residual.

tables.note: A price LIST, not a receipt. `price` is bigint cents handed to Stripe as unit_amount; nothing here records that anybody paid it.

A mirror of Stripe, including plan_snapshot_* — the frozen record of what the customer agreed to pay. Oxy's under ADR 0005; the entitlement read model consumes it through findActiveSubscriptions, which writes nothing. One writer is not a Stripe mirror: lib/seed-comped-accounts.ts grants a comped username the most expensive plan of each product as a synthetic comp_<userId>_<product> row, at the deploy boundary.

writers.entrypoint: POST /billing/webhook — customer.subscription.created/updated, checkout.session.completed (subscription mode) and invoice.payment_succeeded, all funnelling through handleSubscriptionUpdate. Also the comp grant at the DEPLOY boundary: scripts/seed.ts runs lib/seed-comped-accounts.ts on every release, which resolves the comped username through Oxy and writes a synthetic comp_<userId>_<product> row so that account holds the most expensive plan of each product. It is a PLAN grant that moves no money — plan_snapshot_price is 0 and no transaction is written — and the comp_ prefix is what lets routes/billing.ts refuse to hand the id to Stripe.

POST /billing/subscription/cancel, POST /billing/subscription/change-plan, and the webhook's customer.subscription.deleted and invoice.payment_failed. Four of the five subscription write sites entitlements.test.ts accounts for.

tables.note: The receipt. Append-only: the repository exports exactly one writer and no update or delete, and migration 0022 makes that structural rather than conventional.

writers.entrypoint: POST /billing/webhook — a credit purchase (checkout.session.completed) and a subscription renewal (handleSubscriptionUpdate). The renewal writes the transaction FIRST as a lock, on the dedup_key generated column, and only then adds credits. Plus the comp grant at the deploy boundary: lib/seed-comped-accounts.ts gives a comped account its plan's monthly credits through the same dedup-keyed lock a Stripe renewal uses, with amount 0 because no money moved.

tables.note: The one table both halves write. See finding.userCreditsIsTheOnlySharedTable.

writers.entrypoint: One direct caller, and thirteen surfaces behind it — see balanceSurfaces. Mints the row with the default free allowance; touches no paid balance.
getRefreshedUserCredits, the balance-display path. A compare-and-set that tops credits_free back to credits_free_limit once a day.

reserveCredits and the under-reserved branch of _adjustReservation — every chat, image, audio, voice, show and agent turn. Consumes the allowance free-first, which is why a request is funded by the free bucket wherever it can be.
None. The ported deductCredits; kept deliberately, see finding.unreachableWriters.
_adjustReservation, when the true cost exceeded the whole remaining balance. Floors the account at zero rather than going negative.

Three callers, and the `type` argument decides which half each is. ENTITLEMENT: lib/credits-manager.ts refunds the unused part of a reservation to 'free'. FINANCIAL: routes/billing.ts adds 'paid' credits on a completed purchase and on a subscription renewal, and routes/referrals.ts grants 'paid' credits to both sides of a referral — a PROMOTIONAL grant landing in the purchased bucket, which is why the bucket alone cannot tell a promotion from a purchase. Plus the comp grant at the deploy boundary: lib/seed-comped-accounts.ts gives a comped account its plan's monthly credits through the same dedup-keyed lock a Stripe renewal uses, with amount 0 because no money moved.
getOrCreateStripeCustomer and the webhook's customer-id backfill. Pure processor linkage.

balanceSurfaces.note: Every non-test module reaching the balance row through lib/user-credits-helpers.ts, which is the one hop between the repository and the product. Listed separately because the writer census sees only the helper: a table-level or writer-level inventory reports ONE caller here and the blast radius is fifteen. Asserted as an exact set. `routes/shows.ts` joined it in #323: creating a show series draws cover art, which is a real image generation and is reserved and settled exactly as the images endpoint does.

readSideEntrypoints.note: Reads are listed because ADR 0005's cutover deletes the write half and must leave these working. None of them writes.
readSideEntrypoints.entitlementReadModel: lib/plan-access.ts — findActiveSubscriptions + getPlans + getPlanFeatures, cached 5 minutes per account. Publishes the contract's ProductEntitlement.
